headline: Carney ‘Disappointed’ by US Envoy’s Election Interference Accusation
author: Nojoud Al Mallees

paragraphs.text: Fri, October 23, 2026 at 7:33 AM EDT 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Prime Minister Mark Carney says he's disappointed to see the US suggesting that Canada has tried to interfere in its elections, and that his government has been very careful to not even be seen as engaging in such activities.

Speaking to reporters Friday in Istanbul, Carney said there is "no merit" to the claims made by the US Embassy in Canada, which recently published a fact sheet with quotes from federal ministers and premiers that the document said "openly describe plans to influence American politics."

"I'm disappointed that their envoy sees that it's his role to make these suggestions," Carney said, adding that Canada has been "very, very careful to not be seen to" interfere in the US's democratic processes.

"Our global affairs group, well in advance of these fact sheets and allegations, has been reminding everybody: be careful who you are even seen with physically in the same place as, so that such unsubstantiated allegations can be made," the premier said.

Bloomberg reported on Thursday that Canadian diplomats working in the US have been directed to stay away from candidates running in the midterm elections, and to keep a low profile to avoid allegations by the Trump administration of political interference.

Carney said while he didn't want to participate in a tit-for-tat response, he suggested the media can judge for itself "the extent to which very, very senior US officials have directly intervened, so to speak, in Canadian sovereignty, Canadian democratic processes, encourage certain outcomes."

The prime minister said his government continues to engage with the Trump administration and remains ready to sit down and negotiate a trade deal that's in both countries' interests. Asked whether a deal could come before the US midterms, Carney said "it's up to the United States."
